extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: An open reasoning dataset containing 1.2 million question-response examples for supervised fine-tuning: 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science datapoints. Reasoning traces and answers are generated using QwQ-32B. The dataset was developed through more than 1,000 controlled data-pipeline experiments and used to train OpenThinker3-7B.
extraction.creator: OpenThoughts project
extraction.citeAs: Etash Guha et al. Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. arXiv:2506.04178v2, 5 June 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions are sourced from existing datasets, StackExchange forums, and PDF documents. The final pipeline uses OpenMath-2-Math for math; StackExchange CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning for code; and StackExchange Physics and an Organic Chemistry PDF pipeline for science. The chemistry pipeline extracts PDF text with Gemini, then uses GPT-4o-mini to extract and refine questions and filter them for answerability and organic chemistry relevance. Sources and pipeline strategies are selected by downstream performance in controlled supervised fine-tuning experiments. Selected questions are filtered, deduplicated where applicable, randomly sampled, and answered 16 times using QwQ-32B.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The Organic Chemistry PDF extraction prompt explicitly allows 'NO ANSWER DETECTED' when a correct solution cannot be determined. The question-refinement prompt addresses missing contextual information, and the answerability-filtering prompt treats questions referring to unavailable figures, equations, or additional text as unanswerable. No overall missing-data rate is reported.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Math questions come from ai2-adapt-dev/openmath-2-math, the MATH subset of OpenMathInstruct2. Code questions come from StackExchange CodeGolf coding puzzles and OpenCodeReasoning competitive programming questions. Science questions come from the Physics StackExchange forum and PDFs from SCP-116K, organic chemistry textbooks, solution manuals, and additional organic chemistry materials.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: In the Organic Chemistry PDF pipeline, GPT-4o-mini is instructed to compare each extracted question with its source text and add missing contextual information before restating the question. It must not include the solution in the added context or question.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: PDF questions with explicitly marked subquestions are split into separate, self-contained questions. Questions are refined using their source text without including solutions. The final pipeline samples 16 teacher responses per question and mixes the resulting examples into 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science datapoints. This domain mixture follows the OpenThoughts2-1M mixture.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Code questions are rated for difficulty from 1 to 10 by GPT-4o-mini using an ICPC rubric, and the hardest-rated questions are retained. Math and science questions are selected by the length of GPT-4.1-mini-generated responses, retaining questions with the longest responses. Math and science questions undergo exact-match deduplication; code questions are not deduplicated. Questions are randomly sampled before final answer generation. Evaluation contamination is removed when a training sample has at least 75% normalized Indel similarity to an evaluation sample or shares a 13-token n-gram with it, using the Qwen2-7B-Instruct tokenizer. The final pipeline performs no answer filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: QwQ-32B generates reasoning traces and final answers, with 16 responses sampled per question across all three domains. GPT-4o-mini supplies numerical difficulty ratings for code-question selection using an ICPC rubric and structured decoding. GPT-4.1-mini generates preliminary responses for response-length-based selection of math and science questions. In the chemistry pipeline, GPT-4o-mini extracts questions, answer choices, and solutions, refines questions, and supplies boolean classifications with reasoning for relevance and answerability filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors evaluated answer-verification and filtering methods, including majority consensus, GPT verification, response-length selection, and fastText classifiers. Across domains, training on all answers performed similarly to or better than filtering, so OpenThoughts3 uses no verification or answer filtering. The 16 responses per question are retained as separate training examples rather than aggregated into a consensus label. Teacher-model experiments selected QwQ-32B based on downstream student performance, although DeepSeek-R1 performed better overall as an evaluated model.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The OpenThoughts project is described as a series of continuous releases progressing through four generations: BespokeStratos-17K, OpenThoughts-114K, OpenThoughts2-1M, and OpenThoughts3-1.2M. Dataset and model artifacts are released through the open-thoughts Hugging Face organization, with project code on GitHub. No update schedule or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The project aims to make reasoning-model training data and recipes publicly available, addressing the limited transparency of proprietary datasets and providing a foundation for community research. Safety evaluations show that reasoning supervised fine-tuning inadvertently degrades the base model's existing safety alignment. OpenThinker3-7B has a 55.5% harmfulness rate on Harmbench and a 5.6% over-refusal rate on XSTEST. It was trained without explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data. The authors identify a reasoning–safety trade-off and suggest incorporating safety-specific datasets in future work.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset and pipeline focus on supervised fine-tuning for math, code, and science reasoning; reinforcement-learning datasets, staged supervised fine-tuning, and curriculum learning were not explored. Pipeline strategies were selected by average benchmark performance across domains rather than domain-specific performance, and cross-domain gains may disappear after mixing domain datasets. Distilled reasoning models, including OpenThinker3-7B, show generalization deficits on simple structure-preserving problem variations. OpenThoughts3 does not verify or filter generated answers, and the resulting model lacks explicit safety-focused training.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and supervised fine-tuning of reasoning language models through distillation of teacher-generated reasoning traces and answers, particularly for mathematics, code generation, and science. The full dataset was used to fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct into OpenThinker3-7B. Dataset subsets were used for controlled data-recipe experiments and scaling studies; a 100,000-example subset was also used to fine-tune Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
